title: Traffic Pulse Allocator — phased pulsing rollout & automatic guardrails
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Problem: Current canary rollouts rely on linear step ramps (e.g., 0->10->25->50), which either take too long to detect regressions or create abrupt load changes that perturb backends. We need a rollout primitive that can: 1) exercise new model variants in short, repeated 'pulses' across the traffic surface to surface latent failures quickly, 2) combine pulse schedules with SLO-aware guardrails and automatic rollback, and 3) be configurable per-route and per-customer.

Goal: Implement the Traffic Pulse Allocator: a policy and runtime component that performs phased pulsing (short bursts of traffic to the candidate variant interleaved with baseline traffic), evaluates metrics during and between pulses, and makes automated decisions (continue, widen, hold, or rollback). The allocator should integrate with the existing rollout controller, emit rich signals to Console dashboards, and expose a simple declarative config schema for PMs and SREs.
acceptance_criteria: Allocator supports a pulse schedule: pulse_duration_ms and cooldown_duration_ms configurable per route
Policy engine evaluates pulse-level metrics (latency P95, 5xx rate, quality score delta) and applies threshold-based decisions
Automatic rollback triggers when guardrail thresholds are breached for two consecutive pulses
Console shows pulse timeline and per-pulse metric deltas for any active rollout
API/SDK accepts new rollout config (pulse schedule + metric guards) and default config validated by unit tests
E2E test simulating a quality regression causes rollback within three pulses in CI harness
design_decisions: Use a two-tier guard: immediate safety (latency 3x baseline or 5xx spike) -> immediate revert of current pulse; cumulative safety (metric delta over last N pulses) -> rollback
Pulse sampling will use probabilistic assignment to spread pulses across user cohorts to avoid creating hotspots; default pulse weight = 8% of route traffic during pulse
Keep pulses short (default 30s) with cooldowns (default 5m) to allow downstream stabilization and metric aggregation
Metric sources: runtime telemetry (latency/5xx), Redwood Optimize quality probes (prompt-based evals) fed as asynchronous signals to the allocator
Expose a declarative YAML/JSON config for pulse schedules and guards; map to existing rollout controller policy DSL to reuse upstream routing code
Avoid heavy-weight per-request state: allocator emits routing decisions via route table updates and uses existing prefix/KV cache invalidation hooks
progress_updates: 2025-02-12: RFC drafted; scope reviewed with PM and SRE. Decision to prototype in a feature branch of rollout-controller
2025-02-18: Spike completed validating probabilistic pulse assignment; latency impact below 1% on internal perf-run. Notes: need to cap concurrent pulses per shard
2025-02-25: Initial prototype merged to integration branch (rollout-controller/pulse-prototype); unit tests added for schedule parsing and guard evaluation
2025-03-01: Integration smoke test with Console timeline rendering implemented; UX requested clearer labeling for 'pulse' vs 'steady' windows (feedback from Design)
2025-03-04: Added automatic rollback backstop for cumulative quality delta; preparing PR for review: github.com/redwood/rollout-controller/pull/4321
notes: Trade-offs: Pulsing increases churn on routing tables; mitigations include sharding pulses and respecting shard affinity
Fallback: if evaluation pipeline (Optimize probe) latency is high, allocator falls back to conservative steady ramp using existing step controller
Open: decide whether to allow user-provided custom probe sets or restrict to verified Optimize probes for enterprise customers
